objects.description: Instance-specific function pointer dispatch table populated by volk for a given VkInstance. Applications can store and call instance-level Vulkan functions from this table instead of relying on global pointers. Unknown entries are padded with PFN_vkVoidFunction placeholders when the corresponding extensions/versions are unavailable.

Device-specific function pointer dispatch table populated by volk for a given VkDevice. Applications can store and call device-level Vulkan functions from this table; members are filled when available for the device and left as PFN_vkVoidFunction padding when not.

functions.name: volkInitialize
functions.description: Initializes Volk by loading the Vulkan loader and setting up global Vulkan entry points. Call this before creating your VkInstance. Returns VK_SUCCESS on success, VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED otherwise.
requirements: Must be called before creating the Vulkan VkInstance (per header comment).
Caller must check the VkResult return value and handle VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED.

functions.name: volkInitializeCustom
functions.description: Initializes Volk using a caller-provided function loader instead of loading the Vulkan loader internally. The handler is used to resolve global Vulkan symbols that do not require an instance (e.g., vkCreateInstance, vkEnumerateInstance*, vkEnumerateInstanceVersion).
requirements: handler must be a valid PFN_vkGetInstanceProcAddr-compatible function capable of loading global Vulkan symbols that require no instance.
Intended as an alternative to volkInitialize; do not call both for the same initialization path.

functions.name: volkFinalize
functions.description: Finalizes Volk by unloading the Vulkan loader (if loaded) and resetting global function pointers to NULL. Optional to call; typically not needed at process exit or if volkInitialize failed.
requirements: Optional to call; not required on process exit or if volkInitialize failed.

functions.name: volkGetInstanceVersion
functions.description: Returns the Vulkan instance version supported by the Vulkan loader. If Volk is not initialized or initialization failed, returns 0.
requirements: Returns 0 if volkInitialize/volkInitializeCustom was not called or failed; callers should handle a 0 result.

functions.name: volkLoadInstance
functions.description: Loads global function pointers using the provided application-created VkInstance. Call after creating the Vulkan instance to populate instance/global-level entry points used via Volk’s global pointers.
requirements: instance must be a valid, application-created VkInstance.
Must be called after creating the Vulkan instance (per header comment).

functions.name: volkLoadInstanceOnly
functions.description: Loads instance/global function pointers using the provided VkInstance but skips loading any device-based function pointers. Use this when you plan to load device functions later via volkLoadDevice.
requirements: instance must be a valid, application-created VkInstance.
Must be called after creating the Vulkan instance.
Skips device-based function pointers; callers must subsequently call volkLoadDevice to load device-level functions if using global pointers.

functions.name: volkLoadDevice
functions.description: Loads device-level function pointers using the provided application-created VkDevice, making them available via Volk’s global pointers. Not suitable for applications that need to use multiple VkDevice objects concurrently.
requirements: device must be a valid, application-created VkDevice.
Not suitable if multiple VkDevice objects are used concurrently; use per-device tables instead (see volkLoadDeviceTable).

functions.name: volkGetLoadedInstance
functions.description: Returns the last VkInstance for which volkLoadInstance() was called, or VK_NULL_HANDLE if volkLoadInstance() has not been called.
requirements: None; may return VK_NULL_HANDLE if no instance was loaded.

functions.name: volkGetLoadedDevice
functions.description: Returns the last VkDevice for which volkLoadDevice() was called, or VK_NULL_HANDLE if volkLoadDevice() has not been called.
requirements: None; may return VK_NULL_HANDLE if no device was loaded.

functions.name: volkLoadInstanceTable
functions.signature: void volkLoadInstanceTable(struct VolkInstanceTable* table, VkInstance instance);
functions.description: Populates a user-provided VolkInstanceTable with function pointers resolved for the given VkInstance. Applications can use this table instead of Volk’s global pointers, which is useful for multi-instance or multi-device scenarios.
requirements: table must point to writable memory for a VolkInstanceTable to receive function pointers.
instance must be a valid VkInstance created by the application.
When using per-instance tables, applications should call through the table instead of global function pointers.

functions.name: volkLoadDeviceTable
functions.signature: void volkLoadDeviceTable(struct VolkDeviceTable* table, VkDevice device);
functions.description: Populates a user-provided VolkDeviceTable with function pointers resolved for the given VkDevice. Applications can use this per-device table to avoid global pointer clashes, enabling safe concurrent use of multiple devices.
requirements: table must point to writable memory for a VolkDeviceTable to receive function pointers.
device must be a valid VkDevice created by the application.
When using per-device tables, applications should call through the table instead of global function pointers.

unharnessable_functions.name: volkInitializeCustom
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires a valid PFN_vkGetInstanceProcAddr handler, which cannot be safely synthesized within the fuzzer without defining executable function pointers.
